answer: Copper Sparrow Relay Agents must route messages through at least two distinct relay nodes that each hold a shared secret derived from a decentralized relic. The relic is a persistent cryptographic root stored on a tamper-evident ledger, updated only when a quorum of existing relays agrees. Each relay signs every forwarded packet using its key pair, binding the path to the relic’s current state. An attacker attempting to simulate multiple agents must compromise or clone both a relay and its associated key, requiring physical access to secure hardware or collusion among independent operators.
